Maria (Sales): Hey team — Acme need final answers for the SIG/CAIQ item on encryption/KMS for the enterprise contract. Deadline EOD Wed. Can we confirm BYOK, HSM support, rotation cadence, and what logs we can provide?

Jonah (Solutions Eng): Short answers first: yes BYOK, yes HSM integration for Private, we do envelope encryption, support AWS/GCP/Azure KMS, rotation of data keys supported. Will follow up with specifics.

Lee (Eng-Security): Adding details: for Hosted we offer customer-managed keys (CMKs) via cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). For Dedicated/Private we can also integrate with customer HSMs via PKCS#11 or cloud HSM instances.

Jonah (Solutions Eng): Quick checklist to put in the SIG: 
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ with modern ciphers (we can document cipher list).
- At-rest: model weights, cached KV, and persistent storage encrypted with envelope encryption.
- KMS: support for CMKs (AWS/GCP/Azure) and customer HSM (PKCS#11).
- BYOK: supported for Dedicated/Private; Hosted supports CMKs where customer controls master key.

Tara (Product): Clarify: Hosted + BYOK — customers provide a CMK in their cloud account and grant Redwood a restricted key policy for encryption/decryption operations. We never export plaintext master keys. For Private, keys can remain entirely in customer VPC/HSM.

Maria (Sales): Can we get a one-paragraph answer we can paste into their security portal and a sample KMS ARN/policy snippet?

Jonah (Solutions Eng): Paste this for portal: "Redwood supports customer-managed master keys (CMKs) via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault. For Hosted deployments customers may provision a CMK in their cloud account and grant Redwood limited Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey permissions. For Dedicated and Private deployments we support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) including integration with on-prem HSMs (PKCS#11) or cloud HSMs; cryptographic material is never exported in plaintext from the customer's KMS/HSM. Data is encrypted at rest using envelope encryption; data keys are rotated periodically and keys are audited via cloud KMS/HSM logs."

Lee (Eng-Security): Sample AWS KMS policy snippet (customer-managed CMK) — put in the risk portal: ```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowRedwoodEncryptDecrypt",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {
        "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::REDF_OK_ACCOUNT:role/redwood-kms-role"
      },
      "Action": [
        "kms:Encrypt",
        "kms:Decrypt",
        "kms:GenerateDataKey",
        "kms:DescribeKey"
      ],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}```
(Replace ARN with the role we provide per-customer in the onboarding docs.)

Jonah (Solutions Eng): Rotation & operational notes: 
- Envelope keys (data keys) are rotated by default every 30 days for Hosted; customers can request different cadence during onboarding for Dedicated/Private.
- Master keys (CMKs) rotation is customer-managed; we recommend enabling automatic rotation for CMKs where supported.
- We never persist plaintext data keys outside ephemeral memory; persistent storage holds only ciphertext.

Lee (Eng-Security): Auditing / logs: 
- For Hosted when CMK is in customer account CloudTrail logs KMS Encrypt/Decrypt and GenerateDataKey calls and those logs can be forwarded to customer's SIEM. 
- For Dedicated/Private we forward detailed key usage logs via syslog/S3/CloudWatch integration as part of the onboarding runbook.

Maria (Sales): Customer asked about FIPS / validated HSMs. Reply?

Lee (Eng-Security): We support customers who require FIPS 140-2/140-3 validated HSMs in Private/Dedicated (depends on deployment & vendor). For Hosted we rely on cloud KMS/HSM FIPS-compatible services (AWS CloudHSM / KMS backed by FIPS validated modules). We'll cite vendor validation docs as needed in the questionnaire.

Tara (Product): Also call out separation of duties and access controls: Redwood enforces role-based access for services that perform KMS operations; only minimal service principals/roles have the ability to call Encrypt/Decrypt and operations are logged. Customer key policies are the ultimate access control for CMKs.

Maria (Sales): They asked whether Redwood ever has access to plaintext keys or can decrypt customer data without key consent. Need a one-line statement.

Lee (Eng-Security): One-line: "Redwood does not have access to plaintext master keys; customer CMKs/HSMs control decryption and we use envelope encryption so Redwood never retains plaintext master keys or exported key material."

Jonah (Solutions Eng): Operational caveat to include in SIG: If customer grants Redwood Decrypt access to their CMK in Hosted, Redwood service will be able to perform runtime decrypt operations necessary to serve requests. Customers can minimize blast radius by scoping key policy to required roles and restricting network/principal conditions.

Maria (Sales): Great. Last ask — can we provide an onboarding checklist for security reviewers?

Jonah (Solutions Eng): Quick onboarding checklist to attach: 
- Confirm deployment model (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
- Provide CMK ARN or HSM connection details (PKCS#11 endpoint + certs)
- Provide IAM role ARN for Redwood service or grant cross-account access
- Confirm key rotation policy and retention requirements
- Confirm logging destination (CloudTrail / S3 / SIEM syslog endpoint)
- Sign off on SLA & termination key handling (on termination we flush caches & provide proof of key revocation/rotation)

Lee (Eng-Security): I'll produce a 1-page FAQ and the vendor-validated HSM docs link. @Maria — suggest sending these as the formal response pack.

Maria (Sales): Thanks all — I'll assemble and send. :thumbsup:
